question.problem:
Find ${lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+4g(t)]$ given that $f(t)$ and $g(t)$ are defined as

$$
\begin{aligned}f(t)=[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{t} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ \frac{{t}^{2}+9}{t+3}\end{aligned}],\,g(t)=[\begin{aligned}t-2 \\ \frac{3t-2}{{t}^{2}-1} \\ {2}^{t}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
question.worked_solution:
First, we find the limit of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}f(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}3{e}^{t} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\operatorname{tan}⁡t \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{{t}^{2}+9}{t+3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3{e}^{0} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡0 \\ \frac{{0}^{2}+9}{0+3}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}\,(t-2) \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}\frac{3t-2}{{t}^{2}-1} \\ {lim}_{t\to 0}{2}^{t}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0-2 \\ \frac{3(0)-2}{{0}^{2}-1} \\ {2}^{0}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use properties of limits to calculate the final result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{t\to 0}[f(t)+4g(t)] & ={lim}_{t\to 0}f(t)+4{lim}_{t\to 0}g(t) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+4[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 8 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ 8 \\ 7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
